questions.prompt: Something unexpected happened, but the app recovered and carried on in a degraded way. Which built-in log level fits?
questions.explanation: Warning is for something unexpected but recoverable (degraded behavior); Error means an operation failed, and Critical is a crash or unrecoverable failure.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson prefer `_logger.LogInformation("User {UserId} uploaded file {FileName}", userId, fileName)` over `_logger.LogInformation($"User {userId} uploaded file {fileName}")`?
options: Interpolated strings can't be written to the console
Message templates are required for `LogInformation` to compile
The template keeps the values as structured data, while interpolation loses structure and may evaluate even when the level is disabled
questions.explanation: Always prefer message templates with placeholders: interpolation loses the structure and may evaluate its expressions (like `ExpensiveSizeCalc()`) even if the log level is disabled.

questions.prompt: Serilog is configured with `.MinimumLevel.Information()`. Which messages does this code write?
questions.explanation: `MinimumLevel` is the lowest severity Serilog records; with Information, the Verbose and Debug events are ignored and Information, Warning and Error are written.

source.section: ### MinimumLevel — What logs are allowed to be written

questions.prompt: With `"Default": "Information"` and `"Override": { "Microsoft": "Warning", "System": "Warning" }`, which logs are written?
options: Your app's Information and above, but only Warning and above from `Microsoft.*` and `System.*`
Only Warning and above from every source
Everything from `Microsoft.*`, and only Warning and above from your app
Only Information logs, from every source
questions.explanation: The default level applies to your app (Information+), while the overrides raise the bar for the very noisy framework categories to Warning+, so EF Core, DI and hosting don't spam the logs.

questions.prompt: Why should `OrderService` take `ILogger<OrderService>` in its constructor rather than a plain `ILogger`?
options: `ILogger<T>` writes to files, while `ILogger` only writes to the console
`ILogger<T>` uses `T` as the log category, and DI can create it automatically; a plain `ILogger` can't be injected automatically
`ILogger<T>` is faster because it skips the minimum level check
questions.explanation: `ILogger<T>` uses `T` as the category (for example `MyApp.Services.OrderService`), which makes per-class filtering easy. With a plain `ILogger`, DI cannot create it automatically and you'd have to use `loggerFactory.CreateLogger(...)`.

source.section: #### What if you use ILogger without type?

questions.prompt: Your code calls `_logger.BeginScope("Order {OrderId}", orderId)`, but the scope's properties never appear in Serilog's output. Which enricher does the lesson say you must not skip?
options: None; scopes work without any enricher
questions.explanation: `FromLogContext` enables scopes (such as a CorrelationId or UserId); the lesson warns that without it, scopes do nothing.
